records.name: Science on Tap Philadelphia
records.summary: A monthly talk series for adults curious about science, history and the natural world, run by a group of Philadelphia museums. Talks take place on a Monday evening at a bar and restaurant in Old City, and the series aims for a lively feel rather than a classroom lecture.
records.what_you_do: Come listen to a speaker on one topic for about an hour, then mix with the crowd afterward.

schedule.text: Monthly talk on the second Monday of the month, 6 to 7 pm for most talks (per the 2026 event listings)

locations.label: National Mechanics bar and restaurant, Old City

cost.text: The series site describes its events as free or low cost. Per-event prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Come to a monthly talk, or write to the series email with questions
first_step.basis: Public talks that need no membership. The series has no beginner program, but anyone can attend.

records.notes: The events page lists 30 talks dated from August 2023 to September 2026, each with its year written. The series site and a 2022 news article describe the audience as adults. The sites disagree on whether five or six museums run it, so the record does not name them.

records.name: Nerd Nite Philly
records.summary: Short, informal talks by several speakers on a wide mix of topics, from science and technology to pop culture, held as an evening event at Philadelphia venues. The site has no posts after May 2022, so check before going.
records.what_you_do: Come listen, or get in touch through the site if you want to give a talk.

schedule.text: Monthly evening events, usually on a Wednesday according to older posts

locations.label: Various Philadelphia venues; the last one listed was The Bourse in 2022

cost.text: A $10 cover was listed for a 2022 event. Current prices are not published on the site.

first_step.how: Ask through the site's contact page about attending or pitching a talk
first_step.basis: Past events were open to the public, and the site invites talk pitches, but no current event is shown.

records.notes: Post dates here come from the web addresses of the posts (2019 to 2022). Event bodies give month and day only, with no year. Status is dormant because no post after May 2022 was found. Confirm the group is still running before treating it as active.

records.name: Joseph R. Lynch Observatory public nights (Drexel University)
records.summary: Drexel's physics department opens its rooftop observatory to the public on the first Wednesday of most months during the school year, weather permitting. Everyone is invited, and the night starts about 30 minutes after sunset.
records.what_you_do: Go up to the observatory roof at a listed time and look through the telescope when the sky is clear. Check the status page first.

schedule.text: First Wednesday of most months during the school year, about 30 minutes after sunset. No public nights July to September. Each night is listed on the status page.

locations.label: Roof of the Main Building, 32nd and Chestnut Streets, Drexel University

cost.text: Cost is not stated on the pages checked.

first_step.how: Check the observatory status page for a listed night, then follow the directions on Drexel's physics page
first_step.basis: Open to everyone, but the status page says a telescope upgrade is under way and a November night depends on it.

records.notes: Neither page shows a year. The status page lists one undated Wednesday, November 4 night, which it makes conditional on a new telescope being installed. The only dated item found about the observatory is from 2019, so confirm before going.

records.name: Osher Lifelong Learning Institute (OLLI) at Temple University
records.summary: A lifelong learning program for adults 50 and older at Temple University. Members take daytime classes in Center City with no tests or grades, and can join day trips and member-run committees.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for classes each term, join member activities, or serve on a volunteer committee that plans trips, reviews instructors or runs the lending library.

schedule.text: Daytime classes, term by term. Fall 2026 classes run from Sept 22 to Dec 4, 2026.

locations.label: Center City office, 1515 Market Street, Suite 417

cost.text: Membership: full year $290; fall only $125; spring only $125; spring and summer $175; summer only $85 (as listed on the Fall 2026 page).

first_step.how: Join as a member online or by paper application, then register for classes. Registration uses a waitlist and a lottery.
first_step.basis: A paid membership comes before course registration, so you cannot see the classes first.

records.notes: An older university page lists the Center City office as Suite 400. The current sign-up page says Suite 417, which the record uses. Fee and term dates come from the Fall 2026 sign-up page.

records.name: Academy of Natural Sciences volunteer program (Drexel University)
records.summary: The Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University recruits adult and teen volunteers for its collections, labs, bird collision monitoring and nature walks. Most roles need a steady weekly schedule for at least a year.
records.what_you_do: Help with specimen collections or lab support, monitor for birds hurt by building collisions and transport them, or support nature walks and community science projects.

schedule.text: Regular weekly shifts, mostly on weekdays. Collections roles run weekdays 9 am to 5 pm. Bird collision monitoring runs April to May and September to November.

locations.label: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University, Philadelphia

first_step.how: Submit the online volunteer application linked from the Academy's sign-up page, then email volunteers@ansp.org about open roles
first_step.basis: An application and a year-long weekly commitment come before you can start, but the way in is clear.

records.notes: The sign-up page is undated; the bird monitoring months come from the page itself. Bird Safe Philly and Lights Out Philly are listed as one of the Academy's roles, so they are covered here rather than in a separate record. A 2026 Academy article surfaced in search but its link redirected and was not read.

records.name: SWE Philadelphia (science fair judging)
records.summary: The Philadelphia section of the Society of Women Engineers recruits its members to judge student projects at local science fairs each spring, after a group briefing on judging.
records.what_you_do: Attend a group session on judging, then score student projects at a spring fair such as the George Washington Carver Science Fair in Philadelphia.

schedule.text: Judging drive each winter for spring fairs. The 2026 fairs ran from March 5 to April 1, 2026.

first_step.how: Watch for the next interest form. The 2026 form closed Feb 13, 2026. Questions go to the outreach email.
first_step.basis: Members only, and volunteering runs through an interest form with a deadline.

records.notes: The judging drive is run for members. Fair dates on the page are written as month and day, and the page body says the fairs are in 2026. The outreach email was read from an obfuscated link on the page.

records.name: Philadelphia Unitarian Society of Humanists (PUSH)
records.summary: A monthly discussion group for atheists, agnostics and other non-religious people, meeting at the Unitarian Society of Germantown in Northwest Philadelphia. It talks through issues that affect non-religious people and works toward a more welcoming congregation.
records.what_you_do: Join a conversation with other non-religious people about the issues that matter to them, and help the group's push for inclusion in the congregation.

schedule.text: Fourth Sunday of each month, after the worship service (listed as 12:15 to 2:30 pm)

locations.label: Daskam Room, Unitarian Society of Germantown

first_step.how: Ask the congregation about joining a meeting, since the page does not say whether non-members can come
first_step.basis: The page does not say whether non-members may attend, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the page is a post dated August 28, 2016. The meeting description is in the present tense but undated. The page's personal contact email belongs to a private person, so it was left out. Confirm the group still meets before listing it as active.

leads_only.name: Philly Skeptics
leads_only.note: Meetup-only group. No own website was found in search, so no facts were recorded. A skeptic discussion group worth a future check on its own pages.

leads_only.name: Greater Philadelphia Thinking Society
leads_only.note: Meetup-only group, not checked. Leads only.

leads_only.name: Socrates Cafe (Plymouth-Whitemarsh)
leads_only.note: Community listing on Patch in the Plymouth Meeting area, outside the city. No group website or date found, so not verified.

leads_only.name: Philly Acts of Science
leads_only.note: Citywide citizen science program listed on SciStarter. Its own website was not found and it was not checked. Citizen science falls under the nature-environment family, so another lane may cover it.

notes: Budget: all 10 WebSearch calls used (cap reached, none left). 24 WebFetch calls used, including 404, 403 and redirect responses. Records: 7 published (Science on Tap, Nerd Nite Philly, Drexel Lynch Observatory public nights, Temple OLLI, Academy of Natural Sciences volunteers, SWE Philadelphia judging, PUSH). Status counts: active 3, probably_active 2, dormant 2. Confidence: high 2, medium 2, low 3. Verdict counts: publish 7, hide 0, not_a_group 0, duplicate 0, out_of_area 0. Dropped after checking the group's own page (no record, no lead): Explore STEM Philly at the Philadelphia Education Fund (philaedfund.org) has no STEM tutor or judge role on its homepage. Its details came only from an undated search snippet. Pennypack Ecological Restoration Trust (pennypacktrust.org) links a Streamkeepers page that has no description, dates or join steps on the homepage. The only description came from a 2017 guide, and the work is nature-environment, not this family. The Temple Carver Science Fair judge page is for an annual fair, not a standing group. The Franklin Institute home page showed no recurring stargazing or adult volunteer program. The Academy of Natural Sciences 2026 journal article redirected (301) and was not followed. Surfaced but not recorded: the Delaware Astronomical Society (Wilmington), Chester County Astronomical Society and West Jersey Astronomical Society are outside the city and were not checked. The Humanist Association of Greater Philadelphia surfaced in search with no URL and was not checked. The Mutter Museum and Science History Institute were not searched because the budget ran out. Philly Skeptics and Greater Philadelphia Thinking Society are Meetup-only, so they are listed as leads with no facts recorded. Prompt-injection note: the Pennypack Trust homepage contained embedded text asking for a directory extract. I treated it as page content and did not follow it. Privacy note: the PUSH page lists a private person's personal email address. It was left out of the record.
